Title: Unhealthy API readings recorded in 10 areas nationwide as of 4pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 10 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
In Sarawak, seven areas recorded unhealthy levels: Serian (178), Samarahan (177), Kuching (174), Sri Aman (162), Sarikei (157), Mukah (152), and Sibu (151).
In Peninsular Malaysia, three areas registered unhealthy readings: Johan Setia (154) and Shah Alam (108) in Selangor, and Cheras (127) in Kuala Lumpur.
Meanwhile, 56 areas recorded moderate API levels, while two areas recorded good air quality.
An API reading from 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
API data is updated hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

Title: Malaysia needs more engineers to keep pace with data centre boom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to accelerate the production of engineers and highly skilled technicians to keep pace with the rapid growth of data centre investments in the country.
Data centre chief consultant Lee Cheng Pay said while Malaysia currently has sufficient local talent to support the industry, the pace of new investments meant more engineers would be needed over the next four to five years.
"Currently, local talent is enough, but with the growth in the country, we need to generate more engineers.
"This is where the opportunity comes from. Private institutions and engineering institutions need to work very hard to strengthen engineering programmes and produce more engineers in the next four to five years to catch up with the industry," he said at a preview of the Engineer & Marvex Exhibition and Conference 2026 here today.
Lee said the influx of foreign engineers during the early stages of Malaysia's data centre development had also helped local engineers gain exposure to advanced technologies and industry practices.
"Slowly, you can see the transition. Foreign engineers work together with Malaysian engineers and they start to pick up the knowledge and technologies."
However, Lee said the industry required a broader talent pool beyond engineers, particularly as data centres involved highly complex power, cooling and operational systems.
The Engineer & Marvex Exhibition and Conference 2026 will be held at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre from Sept 22 to 25, 2026.
The exhibition will span five halls covering 9,700 square metres and showcase more than 1,000 solutions across the mechanical and electrical, and heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC) and refrigeration segments.
The event, to be held alongside Data Centre Exhibition Asia, will also feature live showcases covering data centre infrastructure, battery energy storage systems and HVAC innovation for smart and green buildings.
There will also be more than 100 hours of knowledge sessions involving over 150 local and international speakers. It will be held alongside Data Centre Exhibition Asia.

Title: Civil servant held over alleged RM19k bribes in Pahang
Article:
KUANTAN: A civil servant has been arrested for allegedly accepting about RM19,000 in bribes to help companies and individuals secure tenders and contracts at a government agency in Pahang.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) obtained a five-day remand order until Aug 19 to facilitate investigations.
Magistrate Anis Adlina Abu Johan issued the order after the woman, who is in her 30s and attached to a government agency, was brought before the magistrate's court here today.
An MACC source said the suspect was arrested after she went to the Temerloh MACC office to give her statement at 6.45pm yesterday.
"The suspect is believed to have solicited and received about RM19,000 from several companies and individuals in exchange for helping to secure tenders and contracts at a government agency.
"Checks revealed that the suspect had allegedly committed the offences between 2016 and 2021," the source said.
Pahang MACC director Mohd Shukor Mahmud confirmed the arrest and said the case was being investigated under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009 for soliciting a bribe.
If convicted, offenders face up to 20 years in jail and a fine of RM10,000 or five times the value of the bribe, whichever is higher.

Title: Former Nepal premier Deuba returns home, faces graft probe
Article:
KATHMANDU: Former Nepal prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, facing arrest for alleged corruption, returned home Thursday, six months after leaving for medical treatment abroad.
The veteran leader of the opposition Nepali Congress party waved and smiled as hundreds of supporters lined up the streets leading to Tribhuvan airport in the capital, Kathmandu.
In April, police issued an arrest warrant for Deuba over money laundering charges, making him the latest high-profile figure targeted under the new government of Prime Minister Balendra Shah.
Deuba, 80, who left Nepal in February, has denied the allegations.
Nepal police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle said Deuba's case is being handled by the Department of Money Laundering Investigation.
"We are giving security for him at the airport and to his rally because he is a former prime minister," Kafle told AFP.
Authorities had also issued a warrant for Deuba's wife, former foreign minister Arzu Rana Deuba.
The warrants were issued a month after Shah won a landslide victory on a platform of youth-driven political change in the first elections since deadly protests in September 2025.
Deuba's tenure as president of the Nepali Congress ended in January, after younger members pushed for a leadership change.
Shah's administration has launched a sweeping crackdown on high-profile political figures since coming to power.
Former prime minister KP Sharma Oli and ex-home minister Ramesh Lekhak were arrested briefly in March for their alleged roles in the September protests.
The youth-led uprising was triggered by a brief social media ban but tapped into longstanding frustration over corruption and economic hardship in the Himalayan nation.
Protesters set fire to the parliament building and offices, eventually toppling the government.
Deuba's home was among the buildings torched, and videos of protesters attacking the couple circulated widely online. Bundles of cash were reportedly discovered at the property.
In testimony to a commission investigating the protests, Deuba dismissed videos circulating on social media as potentially fabricated.
"This is a conspiracy, although I do not know who is behind it," he said.
The commission has recommended further investigation into the cash allegedly found at Deuba's home and other properties.

Title: Erosion threatens Tanjung Asam beach in Penang
Article:
BAYAN LEPAS: Coastal erosion is damaging Tanjung Asam beach in Gertak Sanggul, a fishing village on Penang Island's southwestern coast, with parts of its shoreline defence and public facilities at risk.
The beach, once known for its clean sand, has gradually been eroded by strong waves, while sections of the shoreline defence have collapsed.
Fisherman Aim Chin Seng, 35, said the damage had been noticeable for several years but had worsened recently.
He said the impact was clearly visible, with the stone embankment built as a wave barrier badly damaged by strong waves.
"There used to be a platform made of stone structures here to help fishermen manage their boats and land their catch.
"However, it collapsed about three years ago, while the embankment here has also been damaged," he said when met here yesterday.
Aim said rocks tied together to form the wave barrier had also collapsed, making it difficult for fishermen to secure their boats.
He said some fishermen had lodged complaints with their elected representative, seeking a solution to protect the damaged shoreline structure.
"We previously spent more than RM1,000 of our own money to buy cement to repair the structure, but it was damaged again shortly afterwards by strong waves.
"There used to be sand here and people came to enjoy it, but now the area has been covered by erosion. We hope immediate and effective action will be taken for everyone's safety," he said.
Checks found sections of the embankment damaged and riddled with holes, while the shoreline damage had also affected the previously built Pusat Bencana Laut.
About 100m from the fishermen's boat area, two rest shelters believed to belong to the Drainage and Irrigation Department appeared at risk of collapsing.
Their floors were broken after the sand beneath them was washed away by waves, while several supporting pillars were damaged and bent.
A tree was also found close to falling because of the damage.
Visitor Mohd Fauzi Ali, 31, from Pokok Sena, Kedah, said it was his first visit to the beach.
"The erosion is clearly visible and the waves here are quite strong. I am worried that eventually this place will disappear.
"I hope repair work can be carried out for the benefit of visitors," he added.
Another visitor, Osman Yasin, 46, said he had brought family members and friends, including an elderly wheelchair user, to enjoy the beach scenery.
"At first, I did not notice that the rest shelter had been damaged by erosion. It should be repaired immediately so visitors can use it for shelter," he said.

Title: Ong Kian Ming hopes DAP delegates will vote for party to quit cabinet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former DAP member of parliament has expressed hope that delegates at this Sunday's congress will vote for the party to quit Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's cabinet.
Dr Ong Kian Ming said there were three reasons for DAP to remain in cabinet, namely the need to pass Budget 2027, political stability amid economic uncertainty, and preventing Barisan Nasional from pulling support for Anwar, which could trigger an early general election.
However, the former Bangi MP said there was only one compelling reason for DAP to leave the cabinet — to pressure Anwar into delivering political reforms before the next general election.
"The DAP delegates and supporters of PH and the DAP must realise that the PM only responds and reacts when there is strong pressure being put on him, whether it is by an individual, a group of people, an organisation, or certain political circumstances.
"This special congress can serve as a way to remind the PM that the DAP delegates have the power to force the DAP leaders to resign from cabinet and to use this leverage to put pressure on him to deliver on some of Pakatan Harapan's manifesto promises before the end of this parliamentary session," Ong said.
He said that if delegates voted for DAP leaders to remain in the cabinet despite these developments, Anwar could interpret it as a signal that DAP would continue supporting the government until the end of the parliamentary term, regardless of whether substantive reforms were introduced.
"Regardless of the speeches made by the delegates or the demands made by DAP leaders at the special congress or through social media, any leverage that the DAP may have on Anwar will disappear the moment most of the delegates vote to 'remain' in cabinet," Ong said.
Ong said a vote to leave the cabinet would not necessarily require DAP ministers to resign immediately, as the party could negotiate with Anwar to remain until Budget 2027 was passed by both the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara in December.
The party could also seek commitments on key reforms, including a 10-year term limit for the prime minister and an equal parliamentary allocation law.
He acknowledged that leaving the government might not guarantee PH and DAP's return to power after GE16, but said it would allow the party to demonstrate that it was prepared to give up government positions on principle rather than for self-interest.
" I hope the DAP delegates will read this message and vote 'leave' rather than to choose to 'remain'," he said.
DAP delegates will decide at the special congress on Sunday whether the party's five full cabinet ministers and six deputy ministers should step down.

Title: Italy's Meloni has a youth problem as election approaches
Article:
ITALIAN Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government is increasingly unpopular among young voters, opinion polls show, a trend that could prove costly ahead of a national election due next year.
Since taking office in 2022, Meloni has done little on the economic front to increase opportunities for the young, analysts say, while passing a raft of law-and-order measures that often disproportionately affect them.
The result is a disaffection among 18- to 34-year-olds that may be crucial at a 2027 election shaping up as a neck-and-neck race between her rightist coalition and the centre-left opposition.
"Younger voters are clearly leaning towards the centre-left," Lorenzo Pregliasco, head of the Youtrend polling agency, told Reuters.
Meloni's coalition, comprising her Brothers of Italy Party (FDI), Matteo Salvini's League and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani's more moderate Forza Italia, now commands less than 30 per cant of voting support among under-35s, Pregliasco said.
That compares with almost 50 per cent in the same age group for the opposition bloc dominated by the Democratic Party (PD), the 5-Star Movement and the Left-Green Alliance (AVS).
At the peak of Meloni's popularity in 2023, Youtrend polling showed her party alone attracted roughly the same support among young people as the whole ruling coalition does now.
Young Italians also present the same gender gap seen in other European countries, with men tending to vote more for the right and women favouring the left, according to a study last year by Milan's Bocconi University based on data from polling firm SWG.
The sharpest party divides showed support for Meloni's FDI at 15 per cent among 18- to 29-year-old men and just 4.2 per cent among women, while 5-Star was backed by 18 per cent of women under 30, and just 5.1 per cent of men.
Lorenzo De Sio, political science professor at Rome's Luiss University, said the main reason for young people's hostility towards the government was its inertia on economic policy.
[[nid:1510482]]
"Meloni has made no significant economic reforms," he said.
"That is fine if you benefit from the status quo, but very bad for those least protected by it, which often means young people."
Meloni's office declined to answer questions from Reuters for this article.
Italy's employment rate among 15- to 24-year-olds is the lowest in the 21-nation euro zone, Eurostat data shows, and it invests less in education than almost all its partners in the bloc.
A young graduate in Germany earns on average 80 per cent more than an Italian peer, according to the Bank of Italy, and tens of thousands of young Italians leave the country every year in search of better prospects abroad.
The government's approval rating among under-35 voters is just 25 per cent compared with 35 per cent among the overall population, Youtrend data shows.
Meloni also faces competition for what remains of the youth vote in her own ideological camp.
National Future, a far-right opposition party formed in February by former army general Roberto Vannacci is already polling at about seven per cent.
Surveys show its strongest support comes from middle-aged men, but Vannacci also has a significant following among anti-immigrant urban youths who like his pledge to return thousands of migrants to their countries of origin.
"Vannacci is certainly holding up better with young voters than the ruling parties are," Pregliasco said.
The government's security measures have affected a range of groups from prisoners to migrants, but young people have often found themselves in the eye of the storm.
After cracking down on rave parties in Meloni's first law decree four years ago, subsequent government steps have targeted production of so-called "light" cannabis, disruptive street protests, squatters, and juvenile crime.
[[nid:1510481]]
A nationwide student protest dubbed 'No Meloni Day' in November last year saw thousands march against the security decrees, education spending cuts and Meloni's support for Israel in Gaza.
In one of its latest moves the government last month presented a bill to change the rules on the criminal responsibility of minors.
Those aged between 14 and 17 who commit crimes will be considered fully responsible unless proven otherwise, reversing current rules by which a judge must show they understood the implications of their actions.
A 2023 decree toughening sanctions for offending minors has already triggered a 50 per cent rise in the juvenile prison population, according to prisoners' rights group Antigone.
Yet while teenagers are to be fully responsible for their crimes, they cannot receive sex education in school without their parents' written consent, under another government step.
Meloni's failure to attract the young has often been masked by voter apathy. Turnout in Italy is normally low among under-35s, who rather than express their dissatisfaction by voting against the government have simply opted not to vote.
However, this trend reversed abruptly at a referendum in March on a reform of the justice system championed by Meloni.
Some 67 per cent of under-35s cast a ballot, with 60 per cent of them rejecting the reform, compared with an overall turnout of 59 per cent of whom 54 per cent voted 'no'.
Sensing trouble, days before the crucial referendum Meloni had joined an irreverent podcast hosted ​by a popular rapper in a bid to reach younger voters.
"The referendum showed what impact the young can have if they vote en masse," De Sio said. "At the next election they could be decisive."
* The writers are from Reuters

Title: Penang air quality hit unhealthy levels before slight improvement
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Air quality in Penang ranged from moderate to unhealthy today, with the Minden monitoring station recording an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading.
The Penang government said API readings across the state ranged from 60 to 107 between Aug 10 and 13 as regional hotspots increased.
State Environment Committee chairman Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu said the latest 3pm reading at Minden had improved to 97, placing it in the moderate category.
The station recorded an API of 107 at noon and 103 at 1pm, according to the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutants Index Management System (APIMS).
Penang has four automatic air quality monitoring stations in Seberang Jaya, Seberang Prai, Minden and Balik Pulau.
Sundarajoo said Minden and Balik Pulau recorded readings between 57 and 107, while Seberang Prai and Seberang Jaya recorded readings between 66 and 96.
He said three stations remained in the moderate category, while one recorded an unhealthy reading.
Preliminary information from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed 213 hotspots in Sumatra and 835 in Kalimantan between Aug 9 and 11, alongside hotspots detected in several Malaysian states.
It said the increase in hotspots in Sumatra and Kalimantan indicated more significant fire activity in the region.
Sundarajoo, however, said hotspot numbers alone could not determine Penang's air quality, as conditions were also influenced by wind direction and speed, atmospheric conditions and rainfall.
"Intermittent rain has helped maintain air quality at good to moderate levels, while PM10 was the dominant pollutant during the monitoring period but remained at a moderate concentration.
"We urge the public to obtain the latest API readings from official APIMS channels and avoid relying on unverified information on social media.
"We also urge the public to reduce open burning, including burning rubbish, dry leaves and agricultural waste, and report such activities to the authorities," he said in a statement this afternoon.
People, particularly children, senior citizens and those with respiratory-related health problems, should reduce strenuous outdoor activities if API readings rise.
Sundarajoo also advised residents to reduce time spent outdoors, close windows and doors if air quality worsens, and use suitable face masks when outside during periods of increased pollution or haze.
"We also call on the public to avoid unnecessary vehicle use and opt for public transport, carpooling or more sustainable modes of travel where possible.
"The state government, through the DOE and relevant agencies, will continue monitoring air quality and regional hotspots," he added, urging the public not to panic or draw premature conclusions based solely on hotspot numbers, but to refer to the latest official API readings for their respective areas.
Earlier today, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government was
monitoring the situation
and would take further measures if air quality deteriorated to a more critical level.

Title: Gaza cancer patients face rising death rate amid Israeli curbs
Article:
CAIRO: Gaza cancer patients are dying at two to three times the pace they did before the start of the war in the territory, as Israel blocks many from travelling for treatment after destroying the only local specialised facility, Gaza doctors said.
Israel blew up Gaza's specialised cancer hospital last year after saying troops found a tunnel used by Hamas fighters running beneath it.
That means that an estimated 17,000 Gazans with cancer have no local option for chemotherapy or other advanced therapy.
Few Palestinians can afford to travel for treatment, and those who can face Israeli restrictions.
The military imposes strict caps on daily crossings to Egypt, despite a 2025 Israel-Hamas ceasefire deal that requires free movement in and out.
Asked for comment, COGAT, the Israeli military agency that controls access to Gaza, said it coordinates medical evacuations with the World Health Organisation.
To depart, Gazans must have a valid request from a receiving country and pass "required security screening," COGAT said.
The WHO did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
For Khuloud Abu Sahmoud, a Palestinian mother-of-two with advanced ovarian cancer, the wait for treatment abroad has become a race against time as her cancer spreads.
"Every day my disease progresses, and my condition is tragic. My fingernails have all fallen out – I have none left. I am just waiting to die."
Abu Sahmoud, 33, said she has been waiting to exit Gaza for treatment in Egypt or further afield since the ceasefire was struck last October.
In that time, the cancer has spread to her lungs and bones, she says.
COGAT said around 5,800 Gazans needing medical treatment have exited to Egypt since Israel agreed in February to a limited reopening of the Rafah border crossing, largely shut during the war that began in 2023.
"Medical evacuations are in no sense restricted by the State of Israel but are wholly dependent on the receiving country's request; without the official request, COGAT cannot coordinate a patient's leave," COGAT said.
Palestinian health officials said 11,000 people, including patients, had gone through Rafah since it reopened, fewer than half the number that had been expected under the ceasefire deal.
A further 20,000 patients, including 5,000 with cancer, are registered for treatment abroad but not yet permitted to leave, the officials said.
[[nid:1510469]]
The ceasefire ended major fighting but left Israeli forces in control of more than half of Gaza, since expanded to around two-thirds.
Nearly all of Gaza's more than 2 million people live in a Hamas-controlled strip along the coast, mostly in makeshift tents or shelters in damaged buildings.
Before the war, local health services had made advances thanks to investment from abroad and persistence from local doctors, a Reuters investigation found.
But most Gaza hospitals were destroyed or damaged in the war, and those that remain operational have been stripped of up to 70 per cent of essential medical supplies, including those needed for cancer treatment and diagnostic services, doctors said.
Among those killed by Israel during the war were dozens of highly qualified specialists, including cancer experts operating in the Turkish-Palestinian Friendship Hospital, demolished in an Israeli controlled demolition in March 2025.
"We have been recording a significant number of deaths, ranging from three to five daily, because patients are not receiving the chemotherapy needed to save their lives," said Mohamed Abu Selmia, head of Gaza's biggest hospital, Al Shifa.
Sobhi Skaik, a Palestinian surgeon who was head of the Turkish-Palestinian Friendship Hospital, said the death rate before the war was about one to two per day.
Some pre-war statistics put the figure at around 1.7 per day, he said.
He said the rising deaths were due mostly to an absence of local treatment and to border restrictions.
But he also said that cancer itself may be spreading at a faster rate due to the presence of toxic materials from Israeli explosives dropped on Gaza.
There were some 11,000 registered cancer patients in Gaza before the war started following the Oct 7, 2023, Hamas attacks on southern Israel, after which registrations largely stopped, Skaik said.
He estimated that another 6,000 Gazans had likely developed cancer since.
"Some people can be treated if diagnosed in early stages, but they are wandering around the tents sick, unaware, and with no help," Skaik said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 6 Paskal personnel rescued after drifting off course in free-fall exercise
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Six Royal Malaysian Navy Special Warfare Forces (Paskal) personnel were rescued after drifting from their intended landing position during a free-fall exercise in the South China Sea.
The RMN said the personnel were found safe at sea by its vessels.
"The deviation was caused by a sudden change in weather that affected visibility.
"The incident demonstrated the effectiveness of Paskal's continuous and realistic training in preparing its personnel to deal with unforeseen situations," it said in a Facebook post.
The navy added that, besides combat skills, the intensive training had proven to foster high levels of resilience, discipline and survival capabilities in extreme situations.
It also said it was committed to balancing combat readiness with personnel safety to ensure the security of the country's waters.

Title: PublicInvest sees nearly 40pct upside for MSC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) maintained its "Outperform" call on Malaysia Smelting Corp Bhd (MSC) with an unchanged target price of RM3.10, implying a potential upside of nearly 40 per cent from the stock's current price of RM2.22.
The firm noted that MSC's long-standing expertise in mineral mining could position it to benefit from opportunities in Malaysia's developing rare earth industry.
"As of August 2026, tin prices are hovering between US$49,000 and US$57,000 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange. This elevated price level is being sustained by supply concerns in Myanmar and Indonesia, coupled with growing demand from the energy and digital transitions," PublicInvest said in a note.
MSC posted a more than two-fold increase in net profit for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q2 FY26), driven by higher tin prices, stronger sales volumes and improved operational efficiencies.
Net profit rose to RM34 million in the quarter from RM13.95 million a year earlier, while revenue jumped 68.2 per cent year-on-year to RM637.3 million.
PublicInvest said the stronger performance was supported by a 44.7 per cent increase in refined tin sales volume and a 49.1 per cent rise in the average realised tin price to RM208,400 per metric tonne (MT), compared with RM139,800 per MT in the corresponding quarter last year.
"In addition, it achieved operational efficiencies from the consolidation of smelting operations at the Pulau Indah plant and ongoing productivity enhancements in mining," the firm said in a note..
The tin mining segment remained MSC's main earnings contributor, with pre-tax profit rising to RM59.1 million, supported by higher tin production volumes and stronger tin prices.
Meanwhile, the tin smelting segment returned to profitability, recording a pre-tax profit of RM3.8 million compared with a loss before tax of RM9.6 million a year ago.
The turnaround was driven by higher profits from tin intermediate sales and cost savings following the closure of the Butterworth smelting plant.
For the first half of FY26, MSC's results met 56.7 per cent of PublicInvest's full-year earnings forecast and 47.5 per cent of consensus estimates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher remanded over alleged assault involving student, mother in Kelantan
Article:
PASIR MAS: A 54-year-old teacher has been remanded for three days to assist investigations into an alleged assault involving a 14-year-old student and his mother.
The remand order, which expires on Aug 15, was issued by the Pasir Mas magistrate's court this morning.
Police arrested the teacher yesterday after receiving a report from the student's mother.
In her report, the 42-year-old woman claimed her 14-year-old son told her that the teacher had struck him with a cane.
The incident allegedly occurred at the student's school on Aug 11.
The woman said she went to meet the teacher the following day to discuss the incident.
She alleged that the teacher slapped her during the confrontation.
Pasir Mas police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan confirmed the report.
Mazlan said the teacher was brought before the court today and remanded for three days to facilitate investigations.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt using a weapon or other dangerous means.

Title: MSA Media Festival and Awards 2026 brings industry leaders together
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Media Specialists Association (MSA) will host its 2026 Festival and Awards on Aug 14, bringing together media practitioners and industry leaders to discuss the future of Malaysia's media landscape.
This year's event carries the theme "MEDIAVOLUTION: Next is now!", reflecting rapid changes driven by technology, artificial intelligence and evolving consumer behaviour.
355 ENTRIES RECEIVED
A total of 126 finalists progressed to the second round of judging on July 14, where they were assessed by more than 65 industry experts, including senior clients, agency practitioners and industry veterans.
Brands represented include CelcomDigi, Maxis, Proton, KFC, McDonald's, U Mobile, Samsung, Malaysia Airlines, Coca-Cola, Netflix, Maybank and Grab.
The winners will be announced during the Gala Awards night on Aug 14.
TALKS BY INDUSTRY LEADERS
Running from 9am to 1.30pm, the sold-out festival has expanded its capacity to meet demand.
Digital entrepreneur Timothy Tiah, founder of Nuffnang and Colony, will deliver the keynote address, alongside representatives from Google and Meta, Astro's Henry Tan and Big Tree's Muhamad Fariz Mustafa.
A key highlight will be the Great Presidential Debate, where presidents of various industry associations will discuss the impact of technology on the media landscape.
The programme will also feature a CMO Grille involving three leading chief marketing officers.
The event has attracted 13 sponsors despite a challenging advertising landscape.
They include TV Sarawak, Google, Nexxen, OMNiA, Astro, Affinity, Adzymic, Teads, Seni Jaya, WOW Media, BorgRise SVL, Target Media and Silverpush.
OMNiA Agency Solutions chief operating officer Stephanie Wong said the festival provided an important platform for industry collaboration.
"At OMNiA, we believe meaningful industry progress happens when brands, agencies and media come together to exchange ideas and challenge conventional thinking," she said.
Teads head of sales Danial Smurthwaite, a first-time sponsor, said the company was excited to support an event celebrating creativity and innovation.
"Celebrating creativity, innovation and excellence is what drives our industry forward, and we're excited to be part of an event that inspires and recognises the very best," he said.
GROWTH IN ENTRIES
MSA president Sheila Shanmugam said the increase was a significant achievement given the challenges faced by the sector.
"We're delighted by the support we have received from all the member agencies, and our entries have grown 7 per cent compared with 2025, which is a huge achievement when 2026 has been an uncertain year for many," she said.
Organising chairman Sandeep Joseph said the association was grateful for the support from sponsors and looked forward to a programme featuring industry discussions, the CMO Grille and Great Presidential Debate.
MSA will also organise a Pickleball Day and CSR Day as part of its wider activities.
Learn more about the MSA Media Festival and Awards 2026 on its official
website
.

Title: Johor to install 5,000 smart CCTVs across Greater JB to boost security
Article:
JOHOR BARU: The Johor government will install about 5,000 smart closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras across Greater JB over the next five years to boost state security.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the installation of additional smart CCTVs forms part of state efforts to enhance safety.
He said the target covers local authorities under the Greater JB region, comprising the Johor Baru City Council (MBJB), Pasir Gudang City Council (MBPG), Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP), and Kulai Municipal Council (MPKu).
"With more smart CCTVs installed, city residents, tourists, and visitors will feel safer, thereby improving public well-being," he said at a press conference after officiating the Johor Smart City Forum 2026 at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre (TMIYC) in Pasir Gudang near here today.
Jafni said the state will also install more smart traffic lights in high-density areas, particularly in city and town centres, to ease congestion.
He added that smart traffic lights deployed in recent years have proven effective in ensuring smoother traffic flow.
The state government will also roll out more smart streetlights across Johor for public convenience.
"Usually, the public lodges complaints with local authorities when streetlights break down. With smart streetlights, local authorities and contractors receive immediate notifications via smartphone, enabling quicker repairs," he said.
Earlier in his speech, he noted that all 16 local authorities in Johor achieved at least a Level 1 rating in the national Smart City framework.
"Most proudly, MBJB is the only local authority in the country to achieve a Level 3 rating," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Romania begins shutdown of nuclear plant due to low Danube
Article:
BUCHAREST: Romania began Thursday the complete shutdown of its only nuclear plant after water levels in the Danube, used to cool the site, fell to a record low, the national nuclear energy company said.
Nuclearelectrica already shut down last month one of the two reactors at the Cernavoda power plant, which usually generates a fifth of the Eastern European country's total electricity.
The second needed to shut as well "due to the significant and ongoing drop in the water level of the River Danube", it said in a statement.
"Nuclearelectrica SA announces that, on the morning of 13 August 2026, it began the procedures for the controlled shutdown of Unit 2 at the Cernavoda Nuclear Power Plant," it said.
Romania has been trying for days to avert a complete shutdown of the plant's two 700MW reactors.
These included blowing up a rock and sinking four barges filled with rocks into the river to try to divert its flows, with total costs are budgeted at more than two million euros (US$2.3 million).
It is the plant's first shutdown since a 2003 drought, when it had to close for several weeks.
Alternative sources, including from wind power generation, as well as imports, are expected to cover electricity supply, the energy ministry said on Wednesday.
It also reiterating an appeal for "responsible consumption."
Unprecedented heatwaves and rain shortages across Europe this year have caused the level of the Danube to plummet.
Nearly two-thirds of the Danube has recorded flow rates that are the lowest on record for a month of July in 34 years of measurements, according to an analysis published on Monday by the European climate change observatory Copernicus.
The current drought, which is already severe, has been exacerbated by human-induced climate change, according to a report by the World Weather Attribution group of scientists, who warn that the problem is set to worsen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor to emulate Netherlands model in managing strays
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor will emulate the Netherlands' approach to manage stray dogs and cats more effectively, safely, and humanely through collaboration with non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the state government would partner with NGOs to address the issue.
"The approach, as implemented in the Netherlands, involves neutering the dogs to prevent breeding, alongside proper care and feeding," he said.
"We need to collaborate with NGOs who will house these strays in a shelter, rather than leaving them until they become rabid, emaciated, and abandoned."
He said this at a press conference after officiating the Johor Smart City Forum 2026 at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre (TMIYC) in Pasir Gudang here today.
He added that stray animals would be neutered and cared for before being made available for adoption.
Currently, only the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB) operates a shelter housing stray dogs in the district.
"Captured animals will be fed, treated, and cared for before being offered for adoption.
"I will personally visit the centre in September as the facility is nearing completion," he said.
He said prior interactions with animal welfare advocates during past campaigns prompted the recommendation for local authorities to adopt a more structured approach to managing strays.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Commuter rescued after falling onto Gombak LRT tracks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A commuter fainted and fell onto the tracks at Gombak LRT station this morning and was rescued by Rapid KL personnel and auxiliary police.
The incident occurred at 9.05am, prompting the activation of the Platform Intrusion Emergency Stop system and a temporary power shutdown to facilitate the rescue.
Rapid KL said operations personnel and auxiliary police responded immediately to carry out the rescue.
"The affected passenger was successfully assisted off the tracks and taken to the emergency room while awaiting the arrival of an ambulance," it said in a statement today.
The passenger was taken to Tawakal Hospital Kuala Lumpur for further medical examination and treatment.
Rapid KL said train operations resumed at 9.12am after safety checks confirmed the tracks were clear and safe.
It advised passengers to get the latest service updates through Rapid KL's official social media channels.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Passport forgery syndicate busted, RM200,000 found in e-wallet linked to mastermind
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department has busted a passport forgery syndicate believed to have been operating for about a year, with its services allegedly used to circumvent foreign worker health screenings.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said two Bangladeshi men, aged 29 and 32, were arrested during raids at two condominium units in Taman Wahyu, Kampung Batu, Kuala Lumpur, about 11.30am yesterday.
The operation, carried out by the department's Intelligence and Special Operations Division following a week of surveillance, was mounted after questioning three Indonesian men arrested on Aug 5 over passport forgery and alteration activities.
"We believe the two Bangladeshis were key figures in this passport forgery syndicate.
"We believe the syndicate had been operating for about a year," Zakaria told reporters today.
He said the suspected mastermind held a Temporary Employment Visit Pass for the construction sector, while the other suspect had overstayed.
Zakaria said the suspected mastermind had been in Malaysia for about nine years.
Authorities seized two genuine Bangladeshi passports, nine suspected forged Bangladeshi passports, three mobile phones, 700 passport pages and 300 passport covers for various countries believed to be fake.
Also seized were suspected forged immigration stamps for entry at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), as well as exit stamps for Batam, Indonesia, and Dhaka, Bangladesh, along with two laptops and a printer.
Zakaria said investigators also discovered RM200,000 in an e-wallet account belonging to the suspected mastermind, believed to be proceeds from the illegal operation.
He said the syndicate was believed to have targeted foreign workers who had failed or were deemed unfit during Foreign Workers Medical Examination Monitoring Agency (Fomema) screenings.
"The photograph in the passport would be changed, but the identity used would remain that of the original person.
"Someone who is healthy could then attend the medical examination using the identity of the person who was unfit," he said.
The department said the forged passports could also be given fake entry and exit endorsements to create what appeared to be legitimate travel records and deceive enforcement agencies.
Zakaria said the syndicate charged between RM200 and RM300 for each transaction.
He said demand appeared to be substantial, judging from the volume of passport-making materials found.
"They could keep stock for materials to produce up to 2,000 fake passports. This indicates that demand was quite high."
Zakaria said producing a forged passport could take only a few minutes if the syndicate had the necessary equipment and skills.
He said the syndicate did not openly advertise its services, instead relying on freelance agents and personal contacts to secure customers.
Investigators would also probe whether printing companies were used to produce some of the materials.
The operation marked the sixth series of arrests involving syndicates using a similar modus operandi.
Zakaria said investigations were continuing to determine whether other members or networks remained active, including outside the Klang Valley.
The suspected mastermind is being investigated under Sections 55D and 56(1)(d) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while the other man is being investigated under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Immigration officers find fake registered addresses in fraudulent PLKS probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Immigration officers attempting to track down holders of fraudulently issued Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) have hit a snag after finding that registered addresses are also fake.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department conducted several raids at addresses linked to the affected permits as part of ongoing investigations.
However, officers found that information registered under the permits did not correspond with actual physical locations.
We have conducted several raids at several locations, but so far we have not found them.
"Although our system contains certain addresses, when we went to the locations, the premises were different from those stated in the PLKS, and the employer information was also different.
"This means they were using other people's addresses, and the addresses were false. This is among the modus operandi used," he told reporters today.
Zakaria said the department would continue tracing the affected PLKS holders.
He said all PLKS holders identified as having been issued irregularly had been blacklisted in the Immigration Department's system.
"This effectively blocks the permits from being used for online transactions, including renewals or changes of address.
"They can no longer conduct any transactions involving the PLKS. If they have any queries, they will have to refer to the relevant Immigration counters," he said.
Zakaria said the latest arrests linked to the investigation involved three Immigration officers attached to the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex about two weeks ago.
He said no further arrests had been made since then, but investigations remained ongoing.
"If we obtain new information, we will take action," he said, adding that the latest arrests brought the total number of Immigration personnel arrested to 14.
Zakaria said the
department's
immediate focus was identifying and locating the holders of the irregular PLKS despite the false information provided in the system.
Last month, a syndicate believed to have hacked the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to fraudulently process and approve Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) was dismantled following a joint operation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Immigration Department.
A total of 12 people were arrested during the integrated operation, codenamed Op Crack, yesterday.
Those detained comprised two company directors, three foreigners, four Immigration officers, two officers from the department's Information Technology Division and a policeman.
The suspects, aged between their 30s and 40s, were arrested between 2pm and 5pm yesterday at the
MACC
headquarters and the Immigration Department office in Penang.
The syndicate suspected of hacking the system exploited insiders within the Immigration Department to gain access to the system.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Two airlines face issues processing Malaysian passports valid beyond 10 years, says Immigration DG
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Only two airlines have encountered problems processing Malaysian passports with validity exceeding 10 years, says Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban.
He said the issue was confined to the systems used by the two airlines and did not involve foreign immigration authorities rejecting Malaysian passports.
He declined to name the airlines.
Zakaria said Malaysian passports issued with validity of up to 10 years and six months were valid and recognised in accordance with International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) standards.
"There was confusion that our passports were supposedly not being accepted by other countries.
"This is incorrect. We have no problem with acceptance by foreign countries. All countries accept our passports even if their validity exceeds 10 years," he told a press conference.
On criticism from certain quarters over the issue, Zakaria said his department was open to being audited.
He said Malaysia's 10-year passport policy remained in force.
"I believe there has been some confusion because people think that the 10-year passport programme has been suspended," he said.
He said what had been discontinued was the practice of carrying forward up to six months of remaining validity from an existing passport when a new 10-year passport was issued.
Under the previous arrangement, Malaysians renewing passports with more than six months remaining on their existing documents could receive the additional period, resulting in some newly issued passports being valid for up to 10 years and six months.
Zakaria said passports already issued with exactly 10 years' validity were unaffected and could continue to be used.
"Those with passports valid for exactly 10 years have no problem travelling.
"For those whom we have already issued passports with a validity of 10 years and six months, we are offering replacements free of charge," he said.
Zakaria said the discontinuation of passports with a validity of 10 years and six months would remain until the airlines resolved their issues.
Yesterday, it was announced that the Immigration Department had capped the validity of
Malaysian international passports at a maximum of 10 years
with immediate effect, following difficulties faced by some passport holders when checking in with airlines overseas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Putin visit to disputed islands 'unacceptable': Japan PM
Article:
TOKYO: Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit on Thursday to the Kuril islands is "unacceptable", Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said, with Tokyo also claiming the territory.
"This visit... by the sitting Russian president goes against Japan's consistent position on the Northern Territories," Takaichi told reporters, using the Japanese name for the islands, saying Putin's trip "offends the sentiments of the Japanese people and is absolutely unacceptable."
Russian-Japanese relations have long been dogged by tensions over the contested islands, known in Japan as the Northern Territories and seized by the Soviet Union in 1945.
The Kremlin posted a video of Putin on one of the Kurils' four main islands, with Russian media saying he visited a fish-processing plant and was given caviar.
Putin travelled to the Kurils after visiting the nearby Russian island of Sakhalin on Wednesday, where Russia's navy was conducting drills.
In Sakhalin, Putin, 73, held a meeting "on ensuring the security of Russia's eastern borders," RIA Novosti said.
"The Northern Territories... are an inherent part of Japan's territory both historically and under international law, and the government of Japan strongly protests this visit," Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi said in a statement earlier.
Ties have worsened since the full-scale conflict in Ukraine began in 2022, with Japan joining other G7 countries in sanctioning Russia and giving money and non-lethal defence aid to Kyiv.
Putin on Wednesday called Japan's sanctions "unprovoked".
"Japan has identified Russia as a main source of threats. I would like to point out that we are not threatening Japan... On the contrary it has territorial claims against our country," Putin said.
Russia and China have also moved closer, with their navies and air forces conducting joint exercises in areas around Japan, provoking Japanese jets to scramble hundreds of times a year.
North Korea, which this month termed Japan's military build-up a "transformation into a war state", has also sent troops and artillery shells to help Russia's war against Ukraine.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 6 teenagers arrested over armed attack in Kuantan
Article:
KUANTAN: Six teenagers have been arrested following an armed attack at a business premises in Jalan Air Putih here that left two people seriously injured.
The male victims, aged 17 and 19, are receiving treatment at a hospital here, with one requiring surgery.
Kuantan police chief Assistant Commissioner Ashari Abu Samah said the victims lodged a police report claiming they were attacked by a group of men at about 2am on Monday.
"The victims were attacked with sticks and metal rods.
"One victim fractured his right arm and sustained a forehead injury that required surgery, while the other sustained injuries to his head, left arm, shoulder and knee," he said in a statement today.
A Toyota Vios was also damaged in the incident.
Ashari said police, acting on information, arrested a suspect in Alor Akar at about 2pm the following day, before arresting another five teenagers near a basketball court in Bukit Setongkol several hours later.
He said investigations indicated that the incident was believed to have stemmed from a threat by one of the teenagers to set fire to a sports club.
Ashari said the six suspects were remanded until Aug 14 to assist investigations under Section 148 of the Penal Code for rioting with weapons, which carries a penalty of up to five years' imprisonment, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Members of the public with information can contact the investigating officer, Inspector Siti Fatimah Mohd Said, at 09-5652074 or their nearest police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fadhlina urges calm over pupil protection policy concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek has called on educators to remain calm and give the Education Ministry room to explain the School Pupil Protection Policy following concerns raised by various parties.
She said the policy was designed to ensure comprehensive protection for all parties dealing with pupils, prioritising the safety of students, teachers, and the wider school community.
Fadhlina added that the policy provides detailed guidelines on the responsibilities of all parties, as well as necessary procedures should any untoward incident occur.
"I have instructed the Education director-general and the ministry's Legal Adviser to hold a special session with stakeholders to address the concerns raised by teachers.
"The ministry is committed to ensuring that every policy is executed carefully and responsibly to create a safe school environment," she said in a Facebook post today.
The policy, announced via a Professional Circular (SPI) dated July 1, requires staff and external parties with official dealings with schools to sign a School Pupil Protection Policy Compliance Pledge as proof of their commitment to pupil safety.
The SPI outlines five key areas of education reform: mental health, reproductive and social health education, child sexual violence and substance abuse prevention, pupil protection policy, and teacher welfare and pupil voice.
Meanwhile, in a separate statement, the National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP) said it is seeking negotiations with the ministry to have the pledge requirement withdrawn and replaced with more professional measures.
NUTP secretary-general Fouzi Singon said that while the union supports its efforts to keep pupils safe, it considers the pledge requirement inappropriate and detrimental to teachers' ability to provide optimal protection.
He added that the document risks exposing teachers to civil lawsuits in the future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pride in the passport: Reflection ahead of Merdeka
Article:
LETTER:
When you are living far from home on a different continent, meeting someone from the same region of the world can genuinely be an exciting event.
That was how I felt when I recently met a Burmese doctor during the induction for a new rotation.
"I'm from Southeast Asia too," I told her excitedly. When she raised an eyebrow, I clarified, "Malaysia."
We ended up sticking together for the rest of the event and later walked to the train station together.
Somewhere along the way, we got to talking about passports.
She casually remarked that the passport of her home country, which she had long since given up for a British passport, held little value when it came to international travel.
She then said: "But you're Malaysian. Your country's passport is strong too."
As someone who is perhaps a little too interested in passport indexes, I could not resist telling her that Malaysia had come in at number seven this year, just one rung below the British passport and on par with Canada.
"There you go," she said, as though she had just proven her point. The conversation shook loose another memory from a few months earlier.
I had gone to London to visit a couple of friends. While riding the Underground, one of them, an Indian national from West Bengal, asked whether I had been travelling recently.
I began ticking off on my fingers the places I had visited in Europe. When i finished, he shook his head, looked at our mutual friend, who is also Malaysian, and then at me.
"The both of you have no idea how lucky you are to hold Malaysian passports," he said.
"Do you know how hard it is for me to get to most of these countries because of visa issues?"
For the first time, i found myself properly considering something i had possessed since 11 years old and rarely given much thought to.
My little red passport. Something I had treated primarily as a document to be retrieved from a drawer before a journey represented, to somebody else, a freedom of movement he did not possess quite so easily.
And i felt a fierce little surge of pride in my country. It is strange how often we take something for granted until we encounter someone who would have loved to stand in our shoes.
But passport rankings change. Countries rise and fall on indexes. And ultimately, the strength of a Malaysian passport is not really the point of this story.
Instead, as Merdeka approaches, i find myself thinking about my two-year-old nephew.
He shares his birthday month with Merdeka Day, having been born five days before Aug 31. He is a sixth-generation Malaysian on his father's side.
I hope he grows up in the Malaysia that i knew and loved. Perhaps that hope contains some nostalgia.
Living away from Malaysia, i sometimes look homeward with the particular tenderness that distance creates. But I hope it is not entirely wishful thinking.
One day, my nephew may decide to seek other pastures, just as his maternal uncle and paternal aunt have done. Or he may choose to remain in Malaysia and build his life there.
Whatever he chooses, I hope Malaysia will give him every reason to feel that the little red passport he carries represents something worth cherishing.
More than the countries it allows him to enter without first applying for a visa. More than whatever number happens to sit beside Malaysia on an international ranking.
I hope he grows up understanding what it means when he says: 'Saya anak Malaysia.'
And wherever in the world life eventually takes him, i hope he will always be able to say those words with pride and a sense of belonging.
LOSHI RAJEN
Merseyside, England
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Berita Harian's Didik gives teachers, pupils added learning resource
Article:
SEREMBAN: The revival of Berita Harian's (BH) educational pullout, Didik, provides teachers and pupils with valuable supplementary material that connects classroom learning with real-world contexts, says the Negri Sembilan Education Department.
Its Preschool and Primary Unit senior assistant director Halida Yunus said the Special Year 4 Learning Matrix Edition would help foster reading interest, comprehension, critical thinking and awareness of real-world issues among pupils.
She said this reflected modern education, which was no longer confined to textbooks and classrooms.
"This is where materials such as Didik play an important role. The Year 4 Learning Matrix offers an engaging way to incorporate newspaper content into pupils' learning experiences," she said at the handover of Didik newspapers at SK Seremban 2B here today.
"When used under teachers' guidance, newspapers can motivate pupils to read with purpose, think critically and learn more meaningfully."
Also present were the department's Educational Technology Resources Sector assistant director Mohd Aiman Abdol Aziz, New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd chief operating officer Luqman Adrine Ja'afar, BH Group Editor Zulkifli Jalil and SK Seremban 2B headmaster Nur Fairudzaini Zainal Abidin.
BH handed over 400 copies of BH Didik to SK Seremban 2B, making it the first school to participate in the programme following the pullout's relaunch on Aug 4.
Halida commended BH and Media Prima, saying the initiative gave teachers an additional resource to make lessons more engaging and relevant.
"This effort not only adds value to learning but also allows pupils to understand how news is produced, how information is selected and how the media functions in society," she said.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli said BH Didik was specifically designed for Year 4 pupils to help prepare them for the new Year 4 Learning Matrix assessment.
He said the pullout, relaunched on Aug 4, was first published on Jan 23, 1995, and became a popular primary school revision guide featuring exercises, notes, quizzes and educational articles for 25 years.
Its publication was halted in March 2020 following the Covid-19 pandemic and the subsequent abolition of public examinations.
Zulkifli said BH's involvement in educational publishing dates back to Dec 4, 1993, with the launch of its first educational insert, Minda Pelajar, for primary and secondary school pupils.
He said Didik was more than an educational publication, serving as a platform to nurture a reading culture and introduce pupils to information and journalism.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teacher remanded over alleged assault involving student, mother in Kelantan
Article:
PASIR MAS: A 54-year-old teacher has been remanded for three days to assist investigations into an alleged assault involving a 14-year-old student and his mother.
The remand order, which expires on Aug 15, was issued by the Pasir Mas magistrate's court this morning.
Police arrested the teacher yesterday after receiving a report from the student's mother.
In her report, the 42-year-old woman claimed her 14-year-old son told her that the teacher had struck him with a cane.
The incident allegedly occurred at the student's school on Aug 11.
The woman said she went to meet the teacher the following day to discuss the incident.
She alleged that the teacher slapped her during the confrontation.
Pasir Mas police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan confirmed the report.
Mazlan said the teacher was brought before the court today and remanded for three days to facilitate investigations.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt using a weapon or other dangerous means.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Federal Court upholds death sentence of former chef for murdering stepson
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court today upheld the death sentence imposed on a former chef for the murder of his four-year-old stepson in 2015.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang, Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali, and Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali dismissed Mohd Sazly Zamry's final appeal against his conviction and sentence.
Delivering the unanimous decision, Rhodzariah described the appellant's killing of the innocent boy as nothing short of heinous and diabolical.
She added that equally damning was the pathologist's undisputed evidence that the child sustained 29 external injuries to his body and head, which could not have been inflicted by anyone other than the appellant.
"The brutality perpetrated against the defenceless and innocent victim is beyond comprehension and is totally reprehensible, despicable and heinous, which shocked not only judicial conscience but also the collective conscience of our society," she said.
She said the death sentence was the only punishment commensurate with the crime committed by Sazly, 49.
She said the conviction was safe as the prosecution presented strong circumstantial evidence establishing his culpability beyond reasonable doubt.
The court noted that Sazly was the sole custodian of the boy for two weeks while his wife was at work, during which time the child was subjected to constant verbal and physical abuse.
Sazly had also sought a neighbour's help to dispose of the body, claiming the child was knocked down in an accident by an unnamed friend. He later resisted arrest and prevented his wife from opening the door when police arrived.
Witnesses testified that the victim was locked in a room for two weeks, with a rope tied from the inside to the outside of the door, where he was subjected to scolding and beatings. His body was later found in an unused toilet behind the house.
DNA from the victim was found on a cane and a mop handle, while mixed DNA was detected in blood splatters on the wall.
Sazly was convicted and sentenced to death by the Shah Alam High Court on Jan 17, 2020, for killing Aidil Adha, the son of his second wife, at a house in Jalan Sungai Udang, Klang, between 2pm and 6.15pm on Dec 20, 2015.
The Court of Appeal subsequently dismissed his appeal on April 14, 2023.
At the Federal Court hearing, deputy public prosecutor Eyu Ghim Siang urged the court to uphold the death sentence, citing the two weeks of sustained abuse, while defence lawyer Datuk Rozal Azimin Ahmad argued for the sentence to be commuted to imprisonment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry driver fined RM9,000 over eight-vehicle crash in Batu Pahat
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A lorry driver was fined RM9,000 by the magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to careless driving that caused an eight-vehicle pile-up early this month.
Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno handed down the sentence to Md Asmawi Alias, 54, following his guilty plea and after considering his mitigation appeal.
The court also ordered the accused to serve six months' imprisonment if he failed to pay the fine, which he subsequently paid.
In addition, the magistrate ordered details of the conviction to be endorsed on his driving licence.
Asmawi was charged with driving without due care and attention, resulting in an accident at Km128.1 of the North-South Expressway (northbound) at 12pm on Aug 4.
The charge was framed under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum fine of RM10,000 and up to 12 months' imprisonment, alongside endorsement on the offender's driving licence.
According to the facts of the case, police received a report regarding a road accident involving eight vehicles.
Investigations revealed the accused was travelling from Johor Baru to Shah Alam when he encountered traffic congestion.
The accused suddenly lost control of the vehicle, failed to stop, and rammed into seven vehicles ahead.
A Volkswagen Polo was completely wrecked in the collision. Investigations concluded that the accused drove without due care and attention for other road users.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by lawyer Kamarulariffin Nordin from the National Legal Aid Foundation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lawyers group urges MBS to scrap cash for capture dog programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A lawyers' group has urged the Seremban City Council (MBS) to scrap its "cash-for-capture" dog programme, saying it encourages pet theft and exposes the public to unnecessary risks.
Lawyers for Animal Rights (LAR) said MBS's "Program Pemberian Insentif Penyerahan Anjing Terbiar Secara Sukarela 2026" offers RM50 for each adult dog and RM25 for each puppy handed over.
The group said the Veterinary Services Department (DVS) classifies dog catching as hazardous work requiring trained personnel, yet MBS was offering incentives to members of the public to capture stray dogs.
"MBS form Borang SA-02 required applicants to accept responsibility for injuries or risks during capture. MBS knew the risks, but shifted the liability onto the public," LAR said in a statement today.
It said applicants could surrender unlicensed dogs based solely on self-declaration, without proper verification.
"A dog without a licence is not necessarily an ownerless dog. LAR is worried the bounty encourages pet theft without microchip or ownership checks," it said.
LAR also said animal welfare non-governmental organisations specialising in rescue and Trap-Neuter-Release-Manage programmes had been excluded from the initiative.
It called on MBS to withdraw the scheme and disclose its legal authority, budgetary approvals, Animal Welfare Act licensing compliance, capture standard operating procedures and dog disposal plans.
It also urged the Negri Sembilan DVS and the Housing and Local Government Ministry to investigate who approved the scheme and why high-risk dog capture had been outsourced to the public.
Referring to the recent death of a dog named Rocky during a capture operation, the lawyers' group said animal management should be
professional and humane
rather than rely on bounty systems.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rocky's death: Man says viral video sparked threats, backlash
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A 24-year-old man facing intense online backlash and death threats over the death of a dog named Rocky has denied abusing or killing the animal.
Muhammad Shah Hizam said he was distressed by accusations following a viral video alleging he tortured and killed the dog during an operation at Taman Telok Gedong Indah in Klang on July 29.
"I live under extreme pressure, receiving intense criticism and death threats after Rocky's death," he told a #Justiceforshah press conference in Bukit Jelutong here today.
"I do not support cruelty to animals, let alone intend to injure or kill them, nor was I involved in the dog's death. I was there solely to perform an assigned duty."
Also present were lawyers Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, Mahmud Jumaat, and Akif Rusli.
Rafique said his client was acting as a community representative after receiving a written invitation from the Jalan Sama Gagah Rukun Tetangga (KRT) in Taman Teluk Gedong Indah to assist in an official operation with the Klang Royal City Council (MBDK).
"All 50 residents involved that night were fully briefed by MBDK personnel, who demonstrated how to capture stray dogs," Rafique said.
"Furthermore, the catch pole used during the operation was not Shah's personal property, but was supplied by MBDK."
He said chaos erupted when a woman claiming to be the dog's owner intervened.
"Based on what Shah witnessed, the woman suddenly hugged and sat on Rocky while the dog was still alive to prevent it from being taken away," he said.
"A struggle ensued while the loop was still around Rocky's neck, creating a tense and chaotic situation."
Rafique noted that 12 other stray dogs were captured without injury during the operation, with Rocky being the only dog that died as a result of the commotion.
He said following the circulation of an edited, partial video, Shah became a victim of extreme cyberbullying, with his identity exposed and threats made against his family.
He also dismissed a viral X-ray image claiming the dog suffered a broken spine from being beaten, stating they were informed it was fake.
The legal team is documenting all defamatory and threatening comments on social media and will not hesitate to initiate civil legal action, including defamation suits, against those involved.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cough and flu remedies flying off the shelves as Sibu’s haze refuses to clear
Article:
SIBU, Aug 13 — The haze situation in Sibu remained at an unhealthy level today, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) recorded at 152 as of 4pm, unchanged from Wednesday.
Local pharmacist Juliana Ting said demand for cough and flu medication had surged amid the hazy conditions, although there had been no significant increase in demand for eye medication or inhalers.
“Cough, sore throat, flu, headache and fever are among the common health problems experienced by people during unhealthy haze conditions,” she said when met.
Ting said children, the elderly and people with respiratory illnesses were among those most vulnerable to the effects of haze.
She advised asthma and other respiratory disease patients to continue taking their medication as prescribed, monitor their symptoms closely and seek immediate medical attention if their condition worsened.
“Always bring your inhaler if you are asthmatic, especially when going outside,” she advised.
Ting said symptoms such as shortness of breath, chest pain, coughing up blood and wheezing should not be taken lightly and required immediate medical attention.
For those experiencing cough, sore throat or eye irritation, she advised the public to wear masks, reduce outdoor activities and drink sufficient water to stay hydrated.
She said N95 masks were more suitable for filtering fine particles from haze and offered better protection than ordinary masks.
“However, the mask is not 100 per cent protection against haze. It is important to wear it properly, covering both the nose and mouth,” she said.
Ting also cautioned the public against taking medication without proper advice and stressed the importance of checking for any allergies to the medication.
She advised asthma and lung disease patients to keep a sufficient supply of prescribed medication at home, but warned against purchasing cough medication, antibiotics, steroids or inhalers solely as a preventive measure without assessment by a doctor or pharmacist.
Her advice comes as Sibu continues to experience unhealthy air quality, with the API recorded at 152 at 4pm, underscoring the need for residents to minimise exposure to the haze. — The Borneo Post

Title: Fake names, dead phone numbers: How Customs unravelled a RM1m cannabis export plot at KLIA
Article:
SEPANG, Aug 13 — The use of fake sender and recipient addresses, as well as unreachable telephone numbers, was uncovered in an attempt to export 12.675 kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds worth RM1.014 million via courier service to a European country last July.
Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Customs director Aspalila Ag Tuah said the addresses stated on the four packages containing the drugs were identified as being in the Klang Valley, but investigations found that the information was false.
“They used fake addresses and the telephone numbers could not be reached either,” she said at a press conference here today.
However, she said authorities were still investigating the country of origin of the cannabis buds, as Malaysia was not a producer of the drug.
On July 13, the Enforcement Division operations team seized four packages suspected of containing cannabis buds at a mail and courier centre branch.
She said an inspection found that the drugs were concealed in airtight transparent plastic bags placed inside children’s toy boxes and were believed to have been intended for export to a European country.
In a related development, she said the Customs Department was informed that two pieces of luggage containing 47.8 kg of cannabis buds worth RM3.824 million, seized on July 14, had been kept at the Lost and Found section of KLIA Terminal 1 for about a month before being inspected.
Aspalila said the luggage was supposed to have been carried on a flight from Kuala Lumpur to Langkawi but was left unclaimed for 30 days.
Asked whether closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage was being reviewed to identify the individual who left the luggage, Aspalila said all angles would be taken into consideration as investigations were still ongoing, including into the identity and nationality of the individual believed to be linked to the luggage. — Bernama

Title: As air quality turns unhealthy at Minden, Penang exco urges public to limit outdoor activities
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — Air quality in parts of Penang reached unhealthy levels today, with the Minden monitoring station recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 107 at noon before improving later in the afternoon.
Penang housing and environment committee chairman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said the Minden station recorded an API reading of 107 at noon, followed by 103 at 1pm, both within the unhealthy category.
He said the reading subsequently dropped to 97 at 3pm, returning to the moderate category.
“From August 10 to 13, up to 3pm, air quality in Penang was generally in the moderate to unhealthy categories, with API readings ranging from 60 to 107,” he said in a statement today.
Sundarajoo said Penang had four automated air quality monitoring stations operated by the Department of Environment (DoE), located in Seberang Jaya, Seberang Perai, Minden and Balik Pulau.
He said monitoring trends showed that the Minden and Balik Pulau stations recorded readings ranging from 57 to 107, while Seberang Perai and Seberang Jaya registered readings of between 66 and 96.
Three of the four stations remained in the moderate category, while one recorded an unhealthy reading.
Sundarajoo said preliminary information from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed that 213 hotspots were recorded in Sumatra and another 835 in Kalimantan between August 9 and 11.
Hotspots were also detected in several Malaysian states.
He said the increase in hotspots in Sumatra and Kalimantan indicated more significant fire activity in the region.
“The number of hotspots cannot be used as the sole indicator to determine the level of air quality in Penang,” he said.
He said the impact on Penang depended on meteorological conditions, particularly wind direction and speed, atmospheric conditions and rainfall distribution.
“Based on the DoE’s current monitoring, weather conditions influenced by intermittent rainfall have also helped to maintain Penang’s air quality at good to moderate levels,” he said.
Sundarajoo said PM₁₀ was identified as the dominant pollutant during the monitoring period, although its concentration remained at moderate levels.
He advised the public to monitor official API readings through the DoE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) rather than relying on unverified information circulating on social media.
He also urged the public to refrain from open burning, including burning rubbish, dry leaves and agricultural waste, and to immediately report such activities to the authorities.
“Reduce strenuous outdoor physical activities if API readings increase, particularly for sensitive groups such as children, senior citizens and individuals with respiratory health problems,” he said.
He advised the public to reduce the amount of time spent outdoors, keep windows and doors closed, and use appropriate face masks if air quality deteriorated or hazy conditions worsened.
Sundarajoo said the DoE and other relevant agencies would continue monitoring air quality and hotspot activity.

Title: Two directors in Perak plead not guilty to faking Socso job incentive claims
Article:
IPOH, Aug 13 — Two company directors pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to charges of submitting false documents under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 incentive claims two years ago.
Leong Chooi Ying, 47, and Phun Wing Kei, 31, entered their pleas after the charges were read separately before Judge Meor Sulaiman Ahmad Tarmizi.
Leong, a director of MS Solution Management Services and MN Tree Resources, is accused of submitting a false Employee Confirmation Form to a Perkeso officer with intent to deceive.
She allegedly committed the offences on March 14, 2024, and May 5, 2024, at Taman Sri Pengkalan.
Phun, a director of CKIN Management Services and Diligent Cleaning Solution, faces similar charges for submitting false forms to two Perkeso officers with the same intent.
He is accused of committing the offence at No. 30, Persiaran Rishah 25, Taman Silibin Ria, on April 15, 2024, and May 29, 2024.
Their charges were filed under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), which carries a maximum 20-year prison term and a fine of not less than five times the false claim, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
MACC prosecuting officer P. Rubina appeared for the prosecution. Lawyers Damian Yeo Shen Li and Lim Kwang Ching represented Leong and Phun, respectively.
Bail was set at RM7,000 for Leong and RM8,000 for Phun, with one surety each. They were also ordered to report to the MACC monthly, surrender their passports, and avoid contacting witnesses.
Both case mentions were set for Sept 17. — Bernama

Title: Govt to reassess Sosma, refugee policies against current needs, says home minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The direction of the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma) and the issue of refugees require in-depth scrutiny to ensure that policies and measures remain relevant to current developments and national needs, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
