Saifuddin Nasution, who chaired a discussion on the two issues this morning, said neither should be viewed from a single perspective, but instead assessed by taking into account recent developments, challenges on the ground and possible approaches for the future.
“That is why discussion platforms like this are important. We want every measure taken not merely to address immediate needs, but to be practical, well-founded and suited to current circumstances,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Sosma, which was introduced in 2012, provides authorities with special measures to address security offences and replaced the Internal Security Act 1960 (ISA), which was subsequently repealed.
The legislation has previously come under scrutiny, with various parties calling for its repeal or review, particularly concerning its provisions and implementation.
Meanwhile, the issue of refugees, particularly those from Myanmar, has also attracted significant public attention in recent months, amid concerns over national security, humanitarian considerations and the management of refugee communities. — Bernama

Title: MACC’s KWAP eFishery probe is almost done at home — now it’s waiting on overseas banks
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has so far found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing involving corruption or misappropriation in the Retirement Fund Incorporated’s (KWAP) RM163.4 million investment in Indonesian aquaculture firm eFishery.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said, however, that the full findings would only be available after investigators obtained financial information and documents from overseas banks, including those in Singapore and Indonesia.
“To date, 19 individuals have been called to assist in the investigation and have had their statements recorded. They include officers from KWAP, the Finance Ministry and Khazanah.
“No arrests have been made as we have not found it necessary to do so at this stage. However, the investigation is still ongoing,” he told a press conference today.
Abd Halim said investigators were also working to obtain statements from identified witnesses who were currently overseas.
“It can be reported that the domestic investigation is almost complete. We are now awaiting procedures to obtain Mutual Legal Assistance from several countries.
“There should be no issue about the process, but it may take some time as certain legal procedures must be followed,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian police granted access to question pilot detained in Jakarta over drug case, says home minister
Article:
SUBANG, Aug 13 — Indonesian authorities have reportedly allowed Malaysian police investigators to question a Malaysian pilot detained on suspicion of drug trafficking after he allegedly flew from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Jakarta with drugs in his luggage.
According to the
New Straits Times,
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said a Narcotics Crime Investigation Department team sent to Jakarta had been granted access to interview the suspect.
“From the beginning, our investigators were given access by the Indonesian authorities to interview the subject,” he was quoted as saying.
Saifuddin said the investigation was continuing and urged that the team be given time to complete its work.
He added that proposals to strengthen airport security, being studied by a multi-agency team, could be jointly presented with the transport minister at next week’s Cabinet meeting.
The 39-year-old pilot was detained at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 28 after Indonesian authorities allegedly found 70,114 ecstasy pills and four grammes of methamphetamine in his luggage.

Title: Fresh fruit, veg and protein could soon be added to SARA aid, says Zahid
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 13 — Today’s 18th Executive Committee meeting of the National Cost of Living Action Council (NACCOL) conducted an in-depth review of the local white rice roadmap, which includes a transitional framework to cushion the impact on vulnerable groups.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who chaired the meeting, said tackling the cost of living must go beyond supermarket shelf prices to address production costs, supply chains, access to nutritious food, healthcare and education costs, and support for vulnerable groups.
“To address this, the meeting closely reviewed the path forward for local white rice, focusing on balancing the needs of consumers with the survival of local farmers and producers.
“Among the key proposals is a soft-landing transition via subsidised rice, aimed at safeguarding vulnerable households before broader policy changes take effect,” he said in a statement.
Ahmad Zahid said the meeting also agreed to propose expanding the scope of the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid to include fresh produce, such as fruits, vegetables, and fresh protein, for consideration at the main NACCOL meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“This is an important step to ensure government support goes beyond helping people’s spending power to actively improving access to healthier diets,” he added.
The government is taking cost pressures on business, logistics, and agriculture seriously, he said, including the impact of geopolitical developments, uncertainty in West Asia, import compliance costs, and subsidy rationalisation on food production expenses.
“Continuous monitoring of global geopolitical risks, volatility in West Asia, regulatory compliance expenses for imports, and the effects of targeted subsidies on agricultural production costs is essential to prevent these factors from leading to inflationary pressures on consumers,” he stated.
He said relevant agencies had also been asked to refine existing mechanisms, including targeted assistance for farmers, fishermen, and affected groups.
On healthcare, Ahmad Zahid said the meeting reviewed the rollout of 11 Reset strategy initiatives designed to keep private healthcare costs in check while improving access and expanding treatment options for the public.
He noted that this measure aligns with the government’s integrated framework under the Cost of Living Action Plan 2030, which aims to address living expenses across multiple sectors in a coordinated manner rather than through piecemeal actions.
Meanwhile, the government remains committed to keeping education affordable so that cost never stands in the way of developing talent, he said.
“Based on a mapping of 13 tertiary education aid schemes, 62,937 Form Six and university students received assistance last year, amounting to RM589.6 million.
“Such support needs to be reinforced to ensure every child, regardless of background, gets a fair chance at higher education,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Bandar Utama murder trial: Teen in dock says sorry in court over schoolmate’s death
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 13 — A 15-year-old boy, on trial for the murder of a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year, expressed remorse over the incident while testifying in the High Court here today.
The teenager, who was ordered to enter his defence after the prosecution established a prima facie case, chose to give an unsworn statement from the dock.
“He said he was sorry for what happened that caused the death and so on,” defence lawyer Kitson Foong told reporters after the hearing before Judge Adlin Abdul Majid.
Earlier, Foong informed the court that the defence would rely on the expert testimony of a psychiatrist to support a claim of unsoundness of mind under Section 84 of the Penal Code.
Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, from Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, was called as an expert witness under Section 45 of the Evidence Act 1950, to testify on the teenager’s mental state, including the referral process, treatment and clinical findings.
Foong said the defence had questioned the expert on psychiatric terms, such as psychosis and schizophrenia, in addition to the written report already filed.
The final witness for today, the doctor, testified that the teenager had suffered from delusions and mental illness for about five years.
Foong added that the expert believed a long treatment gap could worsen mental illness, especially when it begins in childhood.
His testimony resumes this afternoon, including possible cross-examination, before the defence closes its case and presents submissions.
The teenager is charged with murdering a 16-year-old girl in a school toilet in Bandar Utama between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14, 2025.
The charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code carries the death penalty. However, under Section 97(1) of the Child Act 2001, the death penalty cannot be imposed on offenders under 18 if convicted.
Instead, under Section 97(2) of the same Act, the court may order the offender to be detained for a period determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the Sultan, or the Yang di-Pertua Negeri. — Bernama

Title: Rehda Institute: One-size-fits-all RM300,000 housing cap needs rethink
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Rehda Institute views positively the government’s indication that affordable housing may move away from the uniform RM300,000 price ceiling towards a more income-based model, saying affordability benchmarks should reflect local household incomes and actual demand.
The research arm of the Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) said the benchmarks should be reviewed periodically, supported by income-based targeting and more location-specific allocation mechanisms.
“Furthermore, housing prices must also recognise actual delivery costs,” it said in a statement following the government’s decision to draft and amend four housing laws under the National Housing Policy (NHP) 2026-2035.
The institute noted that 82 per cent of developers surveyed in its Housing for All study reported that regulated prices for price-controlled housing were below actual development costs due to rising land, construction, labour, compliance and infrastructure costs.
It also supported the government’s emphasis on data-driven planning based on demographics, needs and actual demand.
Rehda Institute said better use of data on household formation, income, demographics, housing stock, vacancy rates, unsold completed units and mobility patterns could help address persistent supply-demand mismatches, unsold housing and abandoned developments.
“It can help avoid overbuilding in weak markets while ensuring genuine housing needs are met in areas of demand. Better data can also enable Malaysia to move from reacting to abandoned projects towards identifying risks earlier and preventing abandonment in the first place,” it said.
It also welcomed the NHP’s specific attention on the ageing population, including housing financing schemes tailored for senior citizens, retrofitting grants to facilitate ageing-in-place and incentives to the private developer for development of liveable senior care centres.
It said the approach was increasingly important as data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) showed that Malaysians aged 65 years and above accounted for eight per cent of the population in 2025, up from 7.6 per cent in 2024.
“Malaysia is on track to become an ‘aged nation’ by 2048, when citizens aged 65 and older reach 14 per cent of the total population. Future housing supply must respond to the different needs of households throughout their life cycle,” it noted.
On housing financing, the institute welcomed proposed measures including the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP), stepped financing, shared ownership and long-term fixed-rate mortgages, particularly as loan eligibility remains a key barrier for aspiring homeowners.
Moving forward, Rehda Institute said it would continue supporting the government through Training, Research and Education, including research and training collaborations and platforms such as the Malaysia-Cambridge Urban Platform (MCUP) to strengthen housing affordability measurement, big data analytics, urban planning and evidence-based policymaking.
In the same statement, Rehda Institute chairman Datuk Jeffrey Ng Tiong Lip was quoted as saying that the NHP 2026-2035 reflected many of the issues the institute had been advocating, particularly demand-driven supply, demographic responsiveness and more flexible financing.
“The next step is to ensure numerical targets remain guided by actual household needs. Ultimately, success should not simply be measured by how many homes are built or owned, but whether Malaysians have access to the right housing, in the right location, under a tenure and financial commitment that they can sustainably afford,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Prima facie proven: Court says Bandar Utama boy must enter defence in schoolmate’s murder
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 13 — The High Court today ordered a 15-year-old boy to enter his defence on a charge of murdering a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year.
Judge Adlin Abdul Majid issued the order after finding that the prosecution had successfully established a prima facie case against the teenager.
Lawyer Kitson Foong, representing the accused, confirmed the court order to reporters after this morning’s proceedings.
The boy is accused of murdering the victim, who was 16 at the time, in the female students’ toilet at a national secondary school in Bandar Utama between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14, 2025.
The charge was brought under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty.
However, under Section 97(1) of the Child Act 2001, the death penalty cannot be imposed on offenders under 18 if convicted.
Instead, under Section 97(2) of the same Act, the court may order the offender to be detained for a period determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the Sultan, or the Yang di-Pertua Negeri.
So far, the prosecution has called three students, teachers, the victim’s mother, a pathologist and a senior investigating officer as witnesses.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutors Raja Zaizul Faridah Raja Zaharudin, Aqharie Durranie Aziz and Ahmad Iqbal Aziz.
As the accused is still a minor and his identity cannot be disclosed, the entire proceedings were held in camera.
On Feb 12, the teenager pleaded not guilty after the charge was re-read to him in Mandarin before Judge Adlin.
On Jan 30, the prosecution obtained the Attorney General’s Chambers’ consent under Section 177A of the Criminal Procedure Code to transfer the case from the Petaling Jaya Magistrate’s Court to the Shah Alam High Court, after a psychiatric evaluation confirmed that the teenager was fit to stand trial.
On Oct 22, 2025, the teenager was charged in the Petaling Jaya Magistrate’s Court with the murder of his schoolmate, between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14, 2025.
No plea was recorded at the time, however, as murder cases fall within the High Court’s jurisdiction.
The proceedings are ongoing. — Bernama

Title: Hoping for a downpour to wash away the smog? MetMalaysia says it won’t be enough for the next five days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The haze situation currently affecting the country is not expected to show any significant changes for the next three to five days, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
MetMalaysia National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre (POCGN) senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said that although rain is forecast to occur in several places, it is not yet able to restore air quality on a large scale.
“From the information we have so far, we have not seen a major change in the situation. We expect the situation to remain almost the same and in the next few days, there will be a little rain compared to the current dry conditions.
“We hope the rain will help, but if the air is very hazy, a little rain may not be able to remove the effects of the haze,” he said when interviewed on Bernama TV’s ‘Focus 15: Cross-Border Haze Threat.’
Commenting further, Maqrun Fadzli said the current haze situation is worse in the west and south of Sarawak, resulting in the closure of more than 100 schools in Serian yesterday, as well as affecting areas in the Peninsula including the Klang Valley.
Maqrun Fadzli said the main factor contributing to the situation is the Southwest Monsoon which usually occurs from May to September, which causes drier conditions and less rain.
“When we don’t get much rain, the weather will be hotter and this hot weather contributes to the risk of burning. From the burning, smoke and what we call haze are produced,” he said.
According to him, MetMalaysia constantly monitors hotspots using satellite images to identify forest fire areas before combining wind direction data to project the movement of smoke and suspended particles.
He said the information is used to identify areas with the potential to experience worse haze conditions and provide predictions of its movement.
Maqrun also advised the public to avoid open burning and reduce outdoor activities to avoid health risks due to unsatisfactory air quality.
As of this afternoon, data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed 10 areas recording unhealthy levels involving Samarahan, Serian, Kuching, Sri Aman, Sarikei, Mukah and Sibu in Sarawak, as well as Johan Setia (Selangor), Cheras (Kuala Lumpur) and Minden (Penang). — Bernama

Title: After calling in 115 witnesses and detaining seven suspects, MACC now weighs foreign forensic help to untangle Tabung Haji probe
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is considering engaging foreign forensic experts to assist in its investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigation involves matters relating to investments, agreements and contracts, and therefore requires detailed forensic examination.
He said the examination would also cover meeting minutes and various documents relating to investment decisions.
“There are a large number of documents involved in this investigation that need to be reviewed and scrutinised. This requires specialised examination as well as expertise.
“Discussions on the appointment of forensic experts are also subject to the costs involved. The forensic experts will also work together with our specialist officers,” he told a press conference here today.
Meanwhile, Abd Halim said that to date, MACC had opened 14 investigation papers and taken several enforcement measures, including arrests, remands and seizures.
He said the investigations involved inspections and searches at 28 premises.
“A total of 115 witnesses have been called in for interviews and had their statements recorded at the MACC office, while seven suspects have been detained, five of whom were remanded,” he added. — Bernama

Title: First AW189 helicopter lands as MMEA steps up patrols, rescues at sea
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Aug 13 — The sovereignty of the country’s 556,285 square kilometres (km) of waters is now strengthened with the receipt of the first of four Medium Lift AW189 helicopters acquired for use by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA).
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the helicopter would enhance the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency’s capabilities in carrying out aerial surveillance, enforcement, search and rescue (SAR) operations, medical evacuation (medevac) and special operations.
He said the acquisition of the sophisticated asset was important in facing the increasingly complex maritime security landscape, including the threat of cross-border crime, encroachment on fisheries resources and smuggling.
“Our maritime zone is very vast, so it is very important for the government to show a strong commitment to support enforcement agencies such as the MMEA,” he said at a press conference after the Malaysian Maritime AW189 Helicopter Reception Ceremony at the Subang Maritime Air Station here today.
Also present were Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman and MMEA director-general Admiral Maritime Datuk Rosli Abdullah.
The procurement of four helicopters worth RM529 million was approved through the Fourth Rolling Plan of the Eleventh Malaysia Plan (11MP), under a five-year contract with manufacturer Leonardo.
The AW189 helicopter has an operating range of up to 1,166km and a maximum speed of 313km per hour, and can operate in various weather conditions while carrying five crew members and 14 passengers for rapid response operations at sea.
Saifuddin Nasution said the company had completed the project on schedule and the remaining three AW189 helicopters were expected to arrive in the country by the end of December.
“Apart from asset empowerment, focus is now also being given to developing personnel capacity to ensure they are skilled in operating the new aircraft’s sophisticated technology,” he said.
With the addition of the new helicopters, MMEA’s air fleet will increase from the current six helicopters to nine by the end of the year, further strengthening the agency’s record in guarding the country’s waters.
As of July 24, MMEA had carried out more than 116,192 inspections, with seizures valued at more than RM4.38 billion, while search and rescue operations had successfully rescued 638 victims in 129 cases.
Meanwhile, he said the government expected to receive another strategic asset, namely a mothership, in the first quarter of next year to further strengthen operations in the deep sea. — Bernama

Title: If you have type O or AB blood, Johor’s Hospital Sultanah Aminah really needs you to come forward this weekend
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 13 — Hospital Sultanah Aminah (HSA) has issued an urgent appeal for type O and AB blood donors as supplies of both types are running low.
In a Facebook post, the hospital’s Transfusion Medicine Department said donors can check the Johor Bahru Blood Donation Campaign Schedule page for locations.
Blood donation drives are also being held at the Johor Blood Donation Centre at Mid Valley Southkey today through Sunday, from 10am to 6.30pm; AEON Mall Bukit Indah today, Saturday, and Sunday from 10am to 3pm; and at the HSA Blood Donation Centre today and tomorrow from 8am to 4.30pm. — Bernama

Title: Two weeks of beatings, 29 injuries: Top court upholds death sentence for man who killed four-year-old stepson in Klang
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 13 — The Federal Court today upheld the death sentence imposed on a former chef for the murder of his four-year-old stepson in 2015.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang, Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali dismissed Mohd Sazly Zamry’s final appeal against his conviction and sentence.
Justice Rhodzariah, delivering the unanimous decision, described the appellant’s killing of the innocent four-year-old boy as nothing short of heinous and diabolical.
She added that equally damning against the appellant was the pathologist’s undisputed evidence that the deceased had sustained 29 external injuries to his body and head, injuries that could not have been inflicted by anyone other than the appellant.
“The brutality perpetrated against the defenceless and innocent victim is beyond comprehension and is totally reprehensible, despicable and heinous, which shocked not only judicial conscience but also the collective conscience of our society,” she said.
Justice Rhodzariah said the death sentence was the only punishment commensurate with the crime committed by Mohd Sazly, 49.
Earlier, she stated that Mohd Sazly’s conviction was safe, as the prosecution had presented strong circumstantial evidence establishing his culpability beyond reasonable doubt.
Justice Rhodzariah said Mohd Sazly was the sole custodian of the deceased for two weeks at the material time, while his wife was at work. During that period, the deceased was subjected to constant verbal and physical abuse.
She further noted that Mohd Sazly had sought a neighbour’s help to dispose of the boy’s body, claiming that the child had been knocked down in an accident by a friend he refused to name.
He also resisted arrest and prevented his wife from opening the door when police arrived.
Mohd Sazly was convicted and sentenced to death by the Shah Alam High Court on Jan 17, 2020, for killing Aidil Adha, the son of his second wife, at a house in Jalan Sungai Udang, Klang, between 2pm and 6.15pm on Dec 20, 2015.
Subsequently, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal on April 14, 2023.
Witnesses testified that the victim was locked in a room for two weeks, with a rope tied from the inside to the outside of the door.
During that time, he was subjected to scolding and beatings. His body was later found in an unused toilet behind the house.
DNA from the victim was found on a cane and a mop handle, while mixed DNA was detected in blood splatters on the wall.
At today’s Federal Court hearing, deputy public prosecutor Eyu Ghim Siang argued for upholding the death sentence, emphasising the two weeks of sustained abuse.
Defence lawyer Datuk Rozal Azimin Ahmad, however, sought to have the sentence commuted to imprisonment. — Bernama

Title: Johor to add 5,000 smart CCTVs across Greater Johor Bahru in five years
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Aug 13 – The Johor government plans to install 5,000 more smart closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras across Greater Johor Bahru over the next five years to improve public safety, said State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor.
The cameras will be installed across four local authority areas as part of Johor’s push to become a Smart State through greater use of technology.
“We are targeting about 5,000 new smart CCTV cameras next year in the Greater JB region, that includes local authorities from the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB), Pasir Gudang City Council, Iskandar Puteri City Council and Kulai Municipal Council.
“With the additional smart CCTV cameras, the residents and visitors will feel safer and this increases the overall well-being of the people,” he told reporters after officiating the Johor Smart City Forum 2026 at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre here today.
Mohd Jafni said the Johor government will also install more smart traffic lights in the state, especially in areas with high traffic flow rates such as in city centres and towns.
He said the use of such technology over the past few years have proven to be successful in managing a smooth traffic flow and reducing traffic congestion in an area.
“In addition, the state government will also install more smart street lights throughout the state for convenience,” he said, adding that the respective local authorities or contractors will be immediately notified of any issues with the smart lights where repair work can be carried out faster.
Earlier, Mohd Jafni announced that all 16 local authorities in the state had managed to obtain a rating of at least Level 1 for the Smart City category in the country.
“Most importantly, MBJB is the only local authority in the country to receive a Level 3 rating,” he said.
Johor is officially recognised as Malaysia’s first Smart State, achieving this milestone five years ahead of its 2030 target.
All 16 local authorities in the state have attained a Level 1 Smart City Early Adopter status, with MBJB leading the nation as the first local authority to reach Level 3 – Leading Smart City status.

Title: Johor wants to give stray dogs a better shot at life, Netherlands-style
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Aug 13 — The Johor government plans to adopt the Netherlands’ widely cited approach to managing stray animals, including sterilisation, shelter care and adoption.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the state government would work with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to address the stray dog and cat population.
“For stray dogs, the approach is similar to the one implemented in the Netherlands where the authorities spays the animal to eliminate unwanted litters, in addition to taking care of their welfare in terms of nutrition.
“So, the plan is to work closely with the NGOs that will place these stray dogs in a dedicated shelter instead of leaving them abandoned and emaciated,” he told reporters after attending the Johor Smart City Forum 2026 at the Tuanku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre here today.
Mohd Jafni said the stray dogs would be neutered and properly cared for before being offered for adoption.
He said the state government welcomed the proposal and was prepared to work with relevant organisations.
At present, he said only the Johor Bahru City Council has a shelter for stray dogs in the district.
He said dogs caught by the council would be fed, treated and cared for before being offered for adoption.
“I will personally visit the shelter this September as I was told the facilities are almost ready,” he said.
Mohd Jafni said interactions with animal lovers during a previous campaign had also prompted suggestions for local authorities to take a more structured approach to managing stray dogs and cats.
He said this would require long-term efforts combining animal welfare measures with shelter care and adoption support.
The Netherlands has been widely credited with eliminating stray dogs from its streets through legislation and subsidised sterilisation programmes.
Its approach to managing stray dogs has been widely cited as a model for other countries, although free-roaming and feral cats remain an ongoing animal welfare and ecological challenge there.

Title: Transport Ministry to refer commingled oil tax issue to MOF for clarification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The Transport Ministry will seek clarification from the Finance Ministry over concerns surrounding the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said today.
Loke said his ministry had yet to be informed of any new taxation involving such cargo, adding that the matter falls under the purview of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and the Finance Ministry.
“This is something which is under Customs and under MOF. We will seek further clarification from MOF,” he told reporters after the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Loke was responding to concerns raised by maritime industry players over uncertainty surrounding the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo at Malaysian ports.
The issue has raised concerns among port businesses, with a maritime expert warning that uncertainty over the tax treatment could affect companies handling such cargo.
Commingling refers to the storage of different oil consignments together in the same shore tank before they are subsequently transferred or exported.

Title: Fadhlina urges calm, says ministry needs space to explain school pupil protection pledge policy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek called on educators to remain calm and give the Ministry of Education (MOE) room to explain the School Pupil Protection Policy, which has recently caused concern among many parties.
She said the policy was designed to ensure comprehensive protection for all parties dealing with pupils, with priority given to the safety of students, teachers and the entire school community.
Fadhlina added that the policy also provides detailed guidelines on the responsibilities of all parties, as well as the actions to be taken should any untoward incident occur at schools.
“I have instructed the Education director-general and MOE’s Legal Adviser to hold a special session with stakeholders to address the concerns raised by teachers.
“MOE is committed to ensuring that every policy is executed carefully and responsibly to create a safe school environment,” she said in a Facebook post today.
The policy, announced via a Professional Circular (SPI) dated July 1, requires staff and external parties with official dealings with schools and their members to sign a School Pupil Protection Policy Compliance Pledge as proof of their commitment to pupil safety.
The SPI outlines five main areas of education reform, namely mental health; reproductive and social health education; child sexual violence and substance abuse prevention; pupil protection policy; teacher welfare; and pupil voice.
Meanwhile, in a separate statement, the National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP)said it is working to hold negotiations with MOE to have the pledge withdrawn and replaced with other, more professional measures.
NUTP secretary-general Fouzi Singon said that while the union supports MOE’s efforts to keep pupils safe and protected at school, it deems the pledge requirement inappropriate and believes it undermines teachers’ ability to provide the best protection.
He further argued that the document risks exposing teachers to civil lawsuits in the future. — Bernama

Title: Alam Flora regrets impact, pledges safety focus as Pantai Hillpark lorry crash probe continues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Alam Flora has pledged its full cooperation with authorities in the probe into a crash involving one of its compactor garbage lorries along Jalan Pantai Murni 1, Pantai Hillpark, yesterday.
In a statement today, Alam Flora informed that the vehicle will be sent for inspection to identify the exact cause of the incident, in line with instructions from the investigating officer.
The company emphasised that the safety and well-being of its workers, contractorsand the public remain its top priority.
“This matter is being treated with the utmost seriousness, and any necessary follow-up actions will be taken based on the investigation’s findings.
“We deeply regret the impact this incident has had on the affected community and remain committed to ensuring high safety standards in all our operational activities,” the statement read.
In the early-morning incident yesterday, a garbage lorry is believed to have experienced a brake failure before losing control and crashing into the perimeter wall of a condominium.
The lorry driver has lodged a report withthe Kuala Lumpur Traffic Police Station, and a breathalyser by the police confirmed that he was not under the influence of alcohol.
The compactor lorry will be sent to the Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (Puspakom) for examination, and the case is being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Perak police probe sexual harassment allegations against PKNPk CEO
Article:
IPOH, Aug 13 — Perak police have opened an investigation into alleged slander involving sexual harassment claims against Perak State Development Corporation (PKNPk) chief executive officer Datuk Redza Rafiq Abdul Razak, following a report lodged by the corporation.
State police chief commissioner Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation was initiated based on the police report lodged by PKNPk over the matter, which had been circulated on social media.
“Police have opened an investigation under Section 507A of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
“The investigation is still ongoing,” he told a press conference at the Perak Police Headquarters here.
Mohd Alwi said police had yet to receive any report from the alleged sexual harassment victim.
He also said police were also awaiting a response from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) regarding the TikTok account linked to the allegations.
“Further investigations would be conducted once police received the information from MCMC,” he added.
Mohd Alwi also said no witnesses had been called to have their statements recorded so far, as police were still trying to identify the owner of the TikTok account.
Yesterday, PKNPk, in a statement, said reports were lodged with the police and MCMC over the dissemination of various allegations against the corporation, its management and certain individuals linked to the organisation.
PKNPk said it was aware of several posts by a Facebook page that had recently been publishing various serious allegations against PKNPk and its management.

Title: Meth, heroin and cannabis worth RM18,500 found inside a Lumut police cell, and a cop's in trouble too
Article:
IPOH, Aug 13 — Three men, including a police constable, were arrested after police seized drugs worth RM18,534 at the Lumut police station lock-up in Manjung.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the drugs were found during an inspection of the lock-up on Tuesday at about 8.30am.
He said police found 16 small plastic tubes containing 109g of methamphetamine, 16 plastic tubes containing 110g of heroin and 23 tubes containing 142g of dried cannabis leaves.
“Following the seizure, we arrested two suspects, in their 40s, who are supposed to be charged for drugs-related offences.
“We also arrested the policeman, in his 30s, who is stationed at the location, to assist the investigation,” he said at a press conference at the Perak police headquarters here.
He said the two drug suspects tested positive for drugs, while all three individuals have been remanded for seven days from August 12 to 18.
Mohd Alwi said police are also investigating how the drugs were smuggled into the lock-up.
He said police take drug abuse and trafficking seriously, including cases involving individuals within police premises or surrounding areas, and would conduct a transparent and thorough investigation to determine appropriate action based on the evidence.
The case is being investigated under Section 39B and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
If convicted under Section 39B, offenders face the death penalty or life imprisonment and whipping of at least 12 strokes, while those convicted under Section 15(1)(a) face a fine of up to RM5,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both.

Title: Transport minister urges commercial vehicle drivers to make RM30 health screening count as fewer than 20 sign up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Fewer than 20 commercial vehicle drivers have taken up the government’s subsidised health screening programme since it was launched last month, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said today.
Loke said the response to the Pemandu Sihat dan Selamat (PSS) initiative remained low despite eligible drivers having to pay only RM30 for a comprehensive health examination, with the Social Security Organisation (Socso) subsidising the remaining RM55.
“I was informed a few days ago that not even 20 people had participated within the one-month period that we had planned,” he said in his speech at the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly and launch of its National Month celebrations here.
The initiative, launched on June 30 and implemented from July 1, targets about 30,000 commercial vehicle drivers aged between 40 and 59 in its initial phase.
Loke said the programme was aimed at improving the health and wellbeing of drivers, particularly those responsible for carrying passengers and operating commercial vehicles.
“When we look after the welfare of drivers, we are actually looking after the safety of road users,” he said.
Speaking to reporters later, Loke said the low participation could be because the programme was still new and greater awareness was needed among drivers.
He said the government had deliberately reduced the cost of the health screening to RM30 through the Socso subsidy, but drivers had yet to take advantage of the initiative.
“It is a good programme that offers subsidies and we have reduced the cost to only RM30 for drivers to pay, but not many have taken the initiative or responded to it,” he said.
Loke urged drivers, particularly older ones, to undergo comprehensive health screenings to identify potential health problems early.
He said conditions such as high blood pressure and diabetes could go undetected if drivers did not undergo proper medical examinations.
Loke said the initiative was also aimed at addressing shortcomings in the existing health certification process for commercial drivers.
While health examinations have long been mandatory, drivers previously only had to submit a medical examination form certified by a doctor or clinic when renewing their vocational licences.
He said this made it difficult to determine whether a thorough physical examination had actually been carried out or not.
“We are not saying it was not done, but it simply could not be determined whether a thorough examination had been conducted,” he said.
Under the new system, doctors at participating clinics will key in their findings directly into an online system, which will then be integrated with JPJ’s MySikap platform.
This means drivers’ health reports will be available when they renew their licences, eliminating reliance on physical forms.
The programme was launched in collaboration with the Human Resources Ministry, Socso, JPJ and the Malaysian Medical Association.
The initial phase involves 500 participating clinics and is scheduled to run from July to December.
The government has allocated RM12.4 million for the programme, including RM7 million from Socso and RM5.4 million from the Finance Ministry.
Loke said the government hoped more drivers would take advantage of the programme and undergo proper health checks rather than simply having forms certified.
“Usually, drivers will just take the form to be certified by doctors. We hope to change that so that they undergo a thorough check-up and find out whether they have any health conditions,” he said.

Title: ‘I am very relaxed’: Loke dismisses talk of final ministry assembly before DAP congress decision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today played down suggestions that this could be his last monthly assembly with Transport Ministry staff ahead of DAP’s crucial vote on Sunday on whether the party should remain in the federal government.
Asked whether today’s ministry assembly could be his final one with ministry staff, Loke dismissed the assumption.
“How do you think it is my last? I have never mentioned that,” he told reporters after the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Asked if he was nervous ahead of the DAP special congress on Sunday, Loke said he was relaxed.
“I don’t know why you ask such a question. I am very relaxed today. I am celebrating with my secretary-general for his birthday. So, after this, we have a birthday celebration for him. Thank you very much,” he said.
Loke’s remarks came three days before DAP delegates are due to vote on a motion that could determine whether the party’s leaders, including its Cabinet members, remain in the government for the rest of the current parliamentary term.
The secret ballot will be held at DAP’s national congress on Sunday, with roughly 4,000 delegates expected to take part. The motion concerns DAP’s participation in the federal government and does not involve the party’s position in Pakatan Harapan.
The vote follows a string of electoral setbacks for DAP and PH, including the party’s loss of all eight seats it contested in the Sabah election last November, followed by further defeats in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
Loke was among the casualties in the latest setback, losing his Chennah state seat after three terms.
Despite the electoral losses, Loke has previously said the decision on whether DAP should remain in government will be left to the delegates.
DAP currently holds five ministerial positions and seven deputy minister posts in the federal administration.
The party has said that even if delegates vote for its leaders to relinquish their government positions, DAP would continue supporting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Parliament until the end of the current term.
For now, however, Loke appears content to wait until Sunday before discussing what comes next.
“After Sunday, we talk,” he said.

Title: Jobstreet: Firms still keen on hiring, job ads grew 33pc year-on-year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Jobstreet said the Malaysian job market appeared resilient in the face of a global supply crisis, as firms continue to show keenness in hiring despite the slight increase in the official unemployment rate.
Job ads on its platform increased by 33 per cent year-on-year as employers appear to be actively looking for talent across the market, Southeast Asia’s largest online employment and career recruitment platform said in a statement today, in line with the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s data that suggests Malaysia’s labour market remains broadly resilient.
“Jobstreet’s platform data reflects continued hiring demand. In H1 2026, job ads increased by 33 per cent year-on-year, showing that employers are still actively looking for talent across the market,” said Nicholas Lam, managing director, Jobstreet by SEEK Malaysia.
Demand remains broad.
Manufacturing, transport and logistics accounted for the largest share of job ads at 12 per cent, followed by accounting at 11 per cent, sales at 10 per cent, engineering at 9 per cent, and administration and office support at 8 per cent, the platform said citing its internal data.
At the same time, DOSM reported that skill-related underemployment remained at 35.2 per cent.
Lim said this points to an ongoing skills-matching challenge: jobs are available, but workers may not always have the right skills for where demand is growing.
“For jobseekers, this makes it increasingly important to understand where opportunities are, build relevant and transferable skills, and position their experience towards areas of demand,” he said.
“For employers, clearer skills requirements and looking beyond traditional qualifications can help widen the available talent pool.”
The labour force expanded by 0.3 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, increasing by 43.7 thousand persons to 17.28 million persons, up from 17.23 million persons in the January to March period, DOSM said.
The Labour Force Participation Rate remained unchanged at 70.9 per cent, the same rate recorded in the preceding quarter.

Title: DAP northern delegates gather to discuss party’s future ahead of Aug 16 national congress
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — About 400 DAP delegates from Penang, Kedah and Perlis attended an engagement session with party secretary-general Anthony Loke Siew Fook and the Central Executive Committee (CEC) leadership here last night.
The session, held ahead of the party’s national congress on Aug 16, served as a platform for delegates to exchange views on party affairs, national issues and the party’s future direction.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, in a Facebook post today, said the session also aimed to strengthen unity among members before the congress in Putrajaya this Sunday.
“A heartfelt thank you to Loke, party leaders, delegates and comrades from the northern region for their participation and valuable insights,” he said.
The upcoming congress is expected to see delegates deliberate on the party’s position and future direction within the Unity Government.
The engagement session also follows a recent decision by the Perak DAP to remain in the Unity Government until the end of the current parliamentary term, citing the need for political stability and the continuation of reforms.
Perak DAP chairman Nga Kor Ming was previously reported as saying that remaining in the government would allow the party to continue contributing to policy-making while fulfilling its mandate to voters. — Bernama

Title: Someone left two suitcases at KLIA’s Lost and Found, Customs found RM3.8m in cannabis — and more hidden in toy boxes
Article:
SEPANG, Aug 13 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Customs foiled four smuggling cases last month, seizing 1.53 million cigarette sticks and 60.47 kg of cannabis buds worth more than RM6.17 million, including duties and taxes.
Its director Aspalila Ag Tuah said two of the cases involved cigarette smuggling at the KLIA Free Commercial Zone, while the other two involved cannabis buds, including 47.8 kg of the drug worth RM3.824 million that was found in two pieces of luggage abandoned at the Lost and Found office in the International Arrival Hall of KLIA Terminal 1.
She said the two pieces of luggage had been booked for a flight from Kuala Lumpur to Langkawi on July 14 but were abandoned by the passengers.
“A scan of the luggage revealed suspicious images, and further inspection uncovered airtight plastic packets believed to contain cannabis buds.
“The airline was called in to assist in tracing the owners of the luggage,” she told a press conference here today.
Aspalila said in another drug case on July 13, the department seized 12.675 kg of cannabis buds worth RM1.014 million that had been concealed in children’s toy boxes.
She said the drugs were found in four packages at the KLIA Customs mail and courier centre and were believed to have been destined for export to a European country via cargo services.
“The syndicate concealed the cannabis in airtight plastic packaging before placing it inside children’s toy boxes to evade detection by the authorities,” she said.
She said both drug cases were being investigated under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Meanwhile, Aspalila said KLIA Customs also foiled two attempts to smuggle a total of 1.53 million cigarette sticks on July 29 and 30, with the cigarettes, duties and taxes valued at about RM1.35 million.
In the first case, she said an inspection of a warehouse at the KLIA Free Commercial Zone on July 29 uncovered 410,000 cigarettes suspected to have been brought in without payment of customs duty under an air waybill from a West Asian country.
Aspalila said the cigarettes were worth about RM102,000, with duties and taxes amounting to RM290,152.
“The consignment was declared as clothing to mislead the authorities and circumvent the requirement for an import permit,” she added.
The following day, she said the department found 1.12 million cigarettes worth RM168,000, with duties and taxes amounting to RM786,400, in a warehouse in the same zone.
She said the cigarettes had arrived from an Asian country for transit and were believed to have been destined for a country in Oceania.
“This time, the consignment was declared as slippers to evade detection by the authorities,” she said, adding that the companies handling the shipments in both cases had been called in to assist in the investigations. — Bernama

Title: Penang’s new air logistics complex set to boost northern cargo capacity, says Anthony Loke
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 13 — The Penang International Logistics Aeropark (Pila) is set to significantly boost air cargo facilities and capacity in Malaysia’s northern region, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke.
He said the project, an expansion of the existing Penang air cargo hub, would provide much greater capacity and strengthen the region’s role as an air logistics centre.
“This will be an expansion, a further expansion, and to make it a Penang Air Logistics Complex. It will be much bigger with increased capacity, and this will definitely boost our air cargo facilities in the northern region,” he told the media after the Ministry of Transport’s monthly assembly here today.
Loke said construction of the project, undertaken by Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) in collaboration with Penang Development Corporation (PDC), had already begun and the project would be launched soon.
“We have invited the Prime Minister to launch the project between MAHB and PDC. It is next to the current Penang cargo hub,” he said.
Loke said the development was part of MAHB’s plans to upgrade its air cargo facilities not only at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), but also in Penang.
“As far as we are concerned, MAHB has a lot of plans to upgrade its air cargo facilities not only in KLIA but also in Penang. Penang will be one major project. There will be expansion of the current air cargo hub.
“All the investment in air cargo hubs will be done by MAHB, not by the government per se. Definitely we will facilitate,” he said.
The Pila project is a private-sector-led investment by MAHB, with the government facilitating its implementation in collaboration with PDC.
This approach is aligned with the government’s broader efforts under Pila to encourage private-sector participation and investment in strategic infrastructure.
In May, it was reported that the boards of PDC and MAHB had approved the formation of a joint venture company, Pila Sdn Bhd, with the agreement signed on April 13, 2026.
The first phase of the project involves the construction of a new free commercial zone-class air cargo warehouse building, which is expected to be completed and operational by 2029.
The development of Pila is expected to accommodate a cargo capacity of up to 500,000 tonnes per year by 2050, with warehouse space exceeding two million square feet. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji reforms must go beyond RCI findings, says BN sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Barisan Nasional (BN) wants all recommendations in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) from 2014 to 2020 to be fully implemented to strengthen confidence among its 10 million depositors.
BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the measures were also necessary to further strengthen TH governance.
“The RCI findings cover governance, power structures, the separation of functions and checks and balances. These should form the basis for strengthening TH, rather than be used for short-term political gain.
“BN welcomes the improvements already undertaken, including the implementation of the RCI recommendations, and believes institutional transformation must continue consistently,” he said in a statement today.
Zambry, who is also Higher Education Minister, said the declassification, ministerial briefing and debate of the RCI report in the Dewan Rakyat demonstrated that transparency had been pursued through legitimate institutional channels.
“BN believes the special parliamentary sitting provided ample room for public scrutiny of the TH RCI report. Transparency has taken place, the debate has been held, and transformation is under way.
“The focus now should no longer be on creating the perception that anyone is trying to hide something,” he said.
Zambry urged all parties to avoid sweeping accusations, political judgement before legal processes were concluded, and narratives that could undermine TH depositors’ confidence without a responsible basis.
He said BN had never sought to restrict public scrutiny of issues involving TH, pointing to BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s early support for the RCI report to be disclosed in Parliament and debated at a special sitting.
“He also proposed broadening the scrutiny to ensure truly comprehensive transparency,” Zambry said.
In the statement, Zambry also called for a comprehensive review of TH’s wider governance history, extending beyond the 2014 to 2020 period examined by the RCI.
“This should include developments and decisions after 2020, such as the role played by Urusharta Jemaah Sdn Bhd since its establishment,” he added. — Bernama
